sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The arrow keys don't move the selected plus — only the HUD bar changes. So the arrow keys are completely irrelevant (or they move a hidden cursor that has no visible effect).
Current understanding:
- Clicking a green plus selects it (a dark gray ring) and displays a gray plus outline at its "destination" cell. Only one plus is selected at a time.
- Clicking a different plus deselects the previous one and selects the new one.
- So what's the goal? Probably: click the destination cell (the gray outline) to move the selected plus there? Or click the plus twice? Or click the destination to "place" the plus.
Let me test: the currently selected plus is #2 (idx2, columns 23-26), and the destination outline is at (18-21, 11-14) — the 2nd cell of the row. Click the destination cell (19,12) and see what happens.

print(len(diffs)); print(diffs)
